words.en: A predecessor is someone who had a job or a position before someone else, or something that comes before another thing in time or in a series.

words.tr: adj. 骇人的； v. “appall”的现在分词；
words.ex: The accident caused an appalling sight.
words.ex_cn: 这场事故造成了一幅骇人的景象。
words.en: If you describe something as appalling, you are emphasizing that it is very bad or unpleasant, and that you find it extremely unacceptable.

words.ex: The team gained momentum after scoring the first goal.
words.ex_cn: 球队在进第一个球后获得了势头。
words.en: Momentum is the ability of something to keep increasing, developing, or being more successful.

words.tr: adj. 极清洁的；一尘不染的；（人）无瑕疵的
words.ex: The kitchen is spotless after she cleaned it.
words.ex_cn: 她打扫后，厨房一尘不染。
words.en: If something is spotless, it is absolutely clean and free from dirt or marks.

words.tr:
n. 寒冷；寒意；
v. 变冷；使冰冷；
words.ex: The chill of the morning made me wear a jacket.
words.ex_cn: 早晨的寒冷让我穿上了夹克。
words.en: A chill is a feeling of coldness, often accompanied by shivering. It can also refer to a feeling of fear or anxiety. As a verb, to chill means to make something cold, or to relax and take it easy.

words.tr: adj. 搁浅的；处于困境的； v. 使搁浅；“strand”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The boat was stranded on the sandbank.
words.ex_cn: 船搁浅在沙洲上。
words.en: Left in a difficult or helpless situation, especially without means of escape or assistance.

words.ex: The signal transmission is clear and strong.
words.ex_cn: 信号传输清晰而强劲。
words.en: The act or process of sending or passing something from one place, person, or thing to another.

words.tr: adv. 不可否认地；无可置疑地
words.ex: He is undeniably the best player on the team.
words.ex_cn: 他无疑是队里最好的球员。
words.en: used to emphasize that something cannot be denied or disputed

words.tr:
n. 极端主义者；过激分子
adj. 极端主义的；过激的
words.ex: The extremist refused to listen to others.
words.ex_cn: 这个极端分子拒绝倾听别人的意见。
words.en: An extremist is someone who has extreme political or religious ideas and is willing to do things that are illegal, violent, or not normal in order to achieve their aims.

words.ex: He is a charismatic leader who inspires everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位有魅力的领导者，能激励每个人。
words.en: A charismatic person attracts, influences, and inspires people by their personal qualities.

words.ex: The chancellor announced a new tax policy.
words.ex_cn: 大臣宣布了一项新的税收政策。
words.en: A chancellor is the head of the government in some countries, or a high-ranking official in a university or other institution.

words.tr:
adj. 极权主义的
n. 极权主义者
words.ex: No example sentences
words.ex_cn: 没有例句
words.en: A totalitarian political system is one in which there is only one political party which controls everything and does not allow any opposition parties.

words.tr:
adj. 丰满的；肥胖的
v. （使）圆胖；（使）鼓起
adv. 噗通地；直接地
words.ex: The baby has plump cheeks.
words.ex_cn: 这个婴儿有圆润的脸颊。
words.en: Having a full rounded shape; chubby.

words.ex: He gave an explicit answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了明确的答案。
words.en: Something that is explicit is expressed or shown clearly and openly, without any attempt to hide anything.

words.ex: His persuasion helped me change my mind.
words.ex_cn: 他的说服让我改变了主意。
words.en: Persuasion is the act of persuading someone to do something or to believe that something is true.

words.ex: The two teams clashed during the match.
words.ex_cn: 这两支队伍在比赛中发生了冲突。
words.en: A clash is a loud, harsh noise, like the clash of cymbals. It can also refer to a conflict or disagreement.

words.ex: The soldiers raided the enemy camp at night.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们在夜间突袭了敌人的营地。
words.en: A raid is a sudden attack on a place by soldiers, police, or other officials, in order to search for something or to arrest someone.

words.ex: He built his endurance by running every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他通过每天早晨跑步来增强耐力。
words.en: The ability to endure an unpleasant or difficult process or situation without giving up.

words.ex: The intruder broke into the house at night.
words.ex_cn: 入侵者在晚上闯入了房子。
words.en: An intruder is a person who enters a place or situation where they are not wanted.

words.ex: He received his father's watch as an inheritance.
words.ex_cn: 他收到了父亲留给他的手表作为遗产。
words.en: Inheritance is money or property which you receive from someone who has died.

words.ex: His disposition is calm and kind.
words.ex_cn: 他的性情平静而善良。
words.en: Someone's disposition is the way that they tend to behave or feel.

words.ex: The arid land has little rain and no trees.
words.ex_cn: 这片干旱的土地降雨稀少，没有树木。
words.en: An arid area of land has so little rain that it is very dry and cannot support much vegetation.

words.ex: The judge gave an unbiased decision.
words.ex_cn: 法官作出了无偏见的判决。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as unbiased, you mean they are fair and not likely to support one particular person or group involved in something.

words.ex: My passport will expire next month.
words.ex_cn: 我的护照下个月到期。
words.en: If something such as a contract or a visa expires, it comes to an end or is no longer valid.

words.ex: His persistence helped him pass the exam.
words.ex_cn: 他的坚持让他通过了考试。
words.en: Persistence is the determination to do something even though it is difficult or other people are against it.

words.ex: He gave a sniff of the flower.
words.ex_cn: 他闻了闻那朵花。
words.en: To sniff is to breathe in air through your nose in a way that makes a noise, especially when you are trying to smell something or when you have a cold.

words.ex: He overheard them talking about the party.
words.ex_cn: 他无意中听到他们在谈论派对。
words.en: To overhear is to hear what someone is saying without them knowing that you are listening.

words.ex: He craves chocolate when he is stressed.
words.ex_cn: 当他感到压力时，他渴望吃巧克力。
words.en: If you crave something, or crave for it, you want to have it very much.

words.ex: He allegedly stole the money.
words.ex_cn: 据他声称，他偷了钱。
words.en: Used to convey that something is claimed to be the case or have taken place, although there is no proof.

words.ex: A shudder ran through her when she saw the snake.
words.ex_cn: 当她看到蛇时，全身战栗了一下。
words.en: If you shudder, you shake with fear, horror, or disgust, or because you are cold.

words.tr:
v. 吼叫；咆哮
n. 吼叫；咆哮
words.ex: The lion let out a loud roar.
words.ex_cn: 狮子发出了一声响亮的咆哮。
words.en: If something roars, it makes a very loud noise, like the sound of a lion.

words.ex: The teacher gave clear instruction on how to solve the problem.
words.ex_cn: 老师给出了如何解决这个问题的明确教授。
words.en: Detailed information telling how something should be done, operated, or assembled.

words.tr: adj. 全神贯注的； v. “engross”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He was engrossed in reading a book.
words.ex_cn: 他全神贯注地看书。
words.en: If you are engrossed in something, you are completely absorbed in it and giving it all your attention.

words.ex: The millennium began in the year 2000.
words.ex_cn: 一千年始于2000年。
words.en: A millennium is a period of one thousand years.

words.ex: The deceptive smile hid his true intentions.
words.ex_cn: 那欺骗性的微笑隐藏了他真正的意图。
words.en: If something is deceptive, it encourages you to believe something which is not true.

words.ex: His rude words provoked her anger.
words.ex_cn: 他粗鲁的话激怒了她。
words.en: If you provoke someone, you deliberately annoy them and try to make them behave aggressively.

words.tr: adj. 令人恐惧的；使人惊骇的；可怕的； v. “horrify”的现在分词；
words.ex: The accident scene was horrifying.
words.ex_cn: 事故现场令人恐惧。
words.en: If you describe something as horrifying, you mean that it is extremely unpleasant and causes great fear or shock.

words.ex: The animals found refuge in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 这些动物在森林中找到了避难所。
words.en: A place or state of safety or shelter from danger, trouble, or difficulty.

words.ex: The court will prosecute him for theft.
words.ex_cn: 法院将因盗窃罪起诉他。
words.en: To prosecute means to institute legal proceedings against someone or to carry on a legal action against a defendant in a court of law. It also means to continue with or carry on an activity or enterprise.

words.tr: v. 繁荣兴旺；茁壮成长；
words.ex: The business flourishes in the new market.
words.ex_cn: 这家企业在新市场中繁荣兴旺。
words.en: If something flourishes, it is successful, active, or common, and developing quickly and strongly.

words.tr: adv. 古怪地；怪异地；反常地；
words.ex: He dressed oddly for the party.
words.ex_cn: 他穿着古怪地去参加派对。
words.en: In a manner that is strange or unusual.

words.ex: The janitor cleans the school every night.
words.ex_cn: 门卫每天晚上打扫学校。
words.en: A janitor is a person whose job is to take care of a building, especially by cleaning it.

words.tr: adj. 相应的； v. 符合；“correspond”的现在分词；
words.ex: Each input has a corresponding output.
words.ex_cn: 每个输入都有一个相应的输出。
words.en: If two things are corresponding, they are similar or equivalent in some way, often because they are connected or related in a particular context.

words.tr: n. 投票者；选民；选举人
words.ex: The voter cast his ballot in the election.
words.ex_cn: 这位选民在选举中投了票。
words.en: A voter is a person who votes or has the right to vote in an election.

words.ex: The fringe of the forest is full of wildflowers.
words.ex_cn: 森林的边缘长满了野花。
words.en: The outer, marginal, or extreme part of an area, group, or sphere of activity.

words.ex: He showed indifference to his friend's problems.
words.ex_cn: 他对朋友的问题表现出冷淡。
words.en: Indifference is the state of being indifferent, especially in the sense of not caring or being uninterested.

words.ex: He criticized others for lying, but his own actions showed hypocrisy.
words.ex_cn: 他批评别人撒谎，但自己的行为却表现出虚伪。
words.en: The practice of claiming to have moral standards or beliefs to which one's own behavior does not conform; pretense.

words.ex: The team unanimously agreed to cancel the trip.
words.ex_cn: 团队全体一致同意取消这次旅行。
words.en: If a group of people are unanimous, they all agree about one particular matter or vote the same way, and if a decision or judgment is unanimous, it is formed or supported by everyone in a group.

words.tr:
n. 捆；束；包
v. 匆匆送走
words.ex: He bought a bundle of newspapers.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一捆报纸。
words.en: A bundle is a number of things that are tied or wrapped together so that they can be carried or stored easily.

words.ex: There was a large influx of tourists during the summer.
words.ex_cn: 夏天期间涌入了大量游客。
words.en: An influx of people or things is a large number of them arriving somewhere at the same time.

words.tr: n. 地平线；思想等的范围；眼界；
words.ex: The sun set below the horizon.
words.ex_cn: 太阳在地平线以下落山。
words.en: The horizon is the line at which the earth's surface and the sky appear to meet.

words.ex: The toy store sells many novelty items for children.
words.ex_cn: 玩具店出售许多为儿童设计的新奇物品。
words.en: The quality of being new, original, or unusual; something new, original, or unusual.

words.tr: adj. 宽厚的；仁慈的；不严格的；
words.ex: The teacher was lenient with students who were late.
words.ex_cn: 老师对迟到的学生很宽厚。
words.en: If you are lenient with someone, you are not strict in the way you treat them, especially when they have done something wrong.

words.ex: He is wholly responsible for the mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他完全对这个错误负责。
words.en: Completely or entirely.

words.tr:
v. 呕吐；吐出；喷涌出
n. 呕吐；呕吐物
words.ex: He felt sick and vomited on the floor.
words.ex_cn: 他感到恶心，就在地上吐了。
words.en: To eject matter from the stomach through the mouth.

words.ex: He tragically lost his life in the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他在事故中悲惨地失去了生命。
words.en: In a manner that is very sad, often involving death or suffering.

words.ex: The storm left only wreckage on the beach.
words.ex_cn: 风暴在海滩上只留下了残骸。
words.en: The remains of something that has been badly damaged or destroyed.

words.tr: adj. 无情的；冷酷的；残忍的；
words.ex: The ruthless boss fired employees without warning.
words.ex_cn: 这位无情的老板未经警告就解雇了员工。
words.en: If you say that someone is ruthless, you mean that you disapprove of them because they are very harsh or cruel, and will do anything that is necessary to achieve what they want.

words.ex: His refusal to listen is irrational.
words.ex_cn: 他拒绝倾听是不合理的。
words.en: If you describe someone's feelings and behavior as irrational, you mean they are not based on logical reasons or clear thinking.

words.tr: adj. 分离的； v. 脱离；拆卸；分离；“detach”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The house is detached from the neighbors.
words.ex_cn: 这所房子与邻居的房子是分开的。
words.en: If someone is detached, they do not have any emotional interest in a situation and therefore can make fair decisions.

words.ex: The judge showed mercy and let him go free.
words.ex_cn: 法官仁慈地让他自由了。
words.en: If someone in authority shows mercy, they choose not to harm someone they have power over, or they forgive someone they have the right to punish.

words.ex: The sailors cleaned the stern of the boat.
words.ex_cn: 水手们打扫了船尾。
words.en: If you describe someone or their behavior as stern, you mean that they are severe or strict.

words.ex: He bought a raincoat, and it rained ironically the next day.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一件雨衣，讽刺的是，第二天就下雨了。
words.en: In a way that is contrary to what is expected and is therefore amusing or strange.

words.ex: The boxes are stored in the warehouse.
words.ex_cn: 这些箱子存放在仓库里。
words.en: A warehouse is a large building where raw materials or manufactured goods may be stored before their export or distribution for sale.

words.ex: He surpassed his brother in math scores.
words.ex_cn: 他在数学成绩上超过了他弟弟。
words.en: If one person or thing surpasses another, the first is better than, or has more of a particular quality than, the second.

words.ex: The monetary policy affects prices.
words.ex_cn: 货币政策影响价格。
words.en: Monetary means relating to money, especially the total amount of money in a country.

words.ex: The nerve in his finger was damaged.
words.ex_cn: 他手指里的神经受到了损伤。
words.en: A nerve is a bundle of fibers that transmits impulses of sensation to the brain or spinal cord, and impulses from these to the muscles and organs. It also refers to the courage or control needed to do something difficult or dangerous.

words.ex: Her cheerfulness made everyone smile.
words.ex_cn: 她的愉快让每个人都笑了。
words.en: Cheerfulness is the quality of being happy and optimistic.

words.tr: n. 可能发生的情况；设想；
words.ex: It's a possible scenario that it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 明天会下雨是一个可能发生的情况。
words.en: A scenario is a description of a possible course of action or events.

words.tr:
n. 猎物；受害者；受骗者；
v. 捕食；坑害；折磨；
words.ex: The lion chased its prey across the plain.
words.ex_cn: 狮子在平原上追逐它的猎物。
words.en: An animal that is hunted and killed by another for food.

words.tr: n. 孤儿；失去生母的幼小动物
words.ex: The boy lives with his uncle because he is an orphan.
words.ex_cn: 这个男孩和叔叔住在一起，因为他是个孤儿。
words.en: An orphan is a child whose parents are dead.

words.ex: The rainwater drains into the street.
words.ex_cn: 雨水排入街道。
words.en: If you drain something, you remove the liquid from it, usually by pouring it away or by allowing it to flow away. If something drains, the liquid flows away from it.

words.ex: Her room is always tidy.
words.ex_cn: 她的房间总是很整洁。
words.en: If you describe something as tidy, you mean that it is neat and arranged in an orderly way.

words.tr: adj. 无望的；凄凉的；荒凉的；
words.ex: The future looks bleak without a job.
words.ex_cn: 没有工作，未来看起来毫无希望。
words.en: If you describe a situation as bleak, you mean that it seems unlikely to improve or get better.

words.ex: He inherited a house from his father.
words.ex_cn: 他从父亲那里继承了一所房子。
words.en: If you inherit something such as a trait, characteristic, or quality, you are born with it, because your parents or ancestors had it. If you inherit money or property, you receive it from someone who has died.

words.ex: He got a vaccine last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周打了疫苗。
words.en: A vaccine is a substance containing a virus or bacterium in a form that is not harmful, given to a person or animal to prevent them from getting the disease that the virus or bacterium causes.

words.ex: Legends say that some heroes are immortal.
words.ex_cn: 传说有些英雄是不死的。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as immortal, you mean that they are so famous or popular that they will be remembered for a very long time.

words.ex: She picked up a thread from the fabric.
words.ex_cn: 她从布料上捡起一根线。
words.en: A thread is a long, thin strand of cotton, nylon, or other fibers used in sewing or weaving. It can also refer to a theme or idea that connects parts of a story or discussion.

words.ex: The change is reversible under normal conditions.
words.ex_cn: 在正常条件下，这种变化是可逆的。
words.en: Capable of being reversed; able to return to an original state or condition.

words.ex: The movie ended with suspense, and no one knew what happened next.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影以悬念结束，没人知道接下来发生了什么。
words.en: Suspense is a state of excitement or anxiety about something that is going to happen very soon, especially something that could be either good or bad.

words.ex: Farmers grow grain like wheat and rice.
words.ex_cn: 农民种植小麦和大米等谷物。
words.en: A grain is a small, hard seed of a food plant such as wheat, rice, or corn, or the plant itself.

words.ex: He loves watching stars and learning astronomy.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢看星星并学习天文学。
words.en: Astronomy is the scientific study of celestial objects, space, and the physical universe as a whole.

words.tr: n. 妥协；互让；意见交换
words.ex: Their friendship needs give-and-take to last.
words.ex_cn: 他们的友谊需要相互妥协才能长久。
words.en: The process by which people reach an agreement or solve a problem by each giving up something that they want.

words.ex: She tied a red ribbon around the box.
words.ex_cn: 她把一条红色的带状物系在盒子上。
words.en: A ribbon is a long, narrow piece of cloth that you use for tying things together or as a decoration.

words.ex: He made a gamble on the horse race.
words.ex_cn: 他在这场赛马上赌了一把。
words.en: If you gamble on something, you take a risky action or decision in the hope of gaining something.

words.ex: He is invariably late for meetings.
words.ex_cn: 他总是开会迟到。
words.en: If something invariably happens or is invariably true, it always happens or is always true.

words.ex: The teacher will formulate a new rule for class.
words.ex_cn: 老师将制定一条新的课堂规则。
words.en: If you formulate something such as a plan or proposal, you invent it, thinking about the details carefully.

words.ex: He lost his job because of his integrity.
words.ex_cn: 他因为正直而失去了工作。
words.en: Integrity is the quality of being honest and having strong moral principles.

words.ex: He went outside regardless of the rain.
words.ex_cn: 他不顾下雨就出去了。
words.en: If you say that someone does something regardless, you mean that they do it without taking account of the possible problems or difficulties.

words.tr: adv. 有系统地；有组织地；
words.ex: He systematically organized his books by subject.
words.ex_cn: 他有系统地按科目整理了他的书。
words.en: in a thorough, methodical, and organized manner

words.tr: v. 接种疫苗；预防接种
words.ex: The doctor will vaccinate the child tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 医生明天会给这个孩子接种疫苗。
words.en: To vaccinate someone is to give them a vaccine, usually by injection, to prevent them from getting a disease.

words.ex: Her resilience helped her recover after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 她的复原力帮助她在事故后恢复。
words.en: The capacity to recover quickly from difficulties; toughness.

words.tr: n. 差额；边缘；净利润；余地；
words.ex: The profit margin is five dollars.
words.ex_cn: 利润差额是五美元。
words.en: The margin is the edge or border of something, or the difference between two amounts, especially the difference between the cost of producing something and the price it is sold for.

words.tr: n. 愚蠢；愚蠢行为；糊涂
words.ex: His stupidity made him fail the test.
words.ex_cn: 他的愚蠢让他考试不及格。
words.en: Stupidity is the quality of being stupid or lacking intelligence.

words.ex: The transition from school to work was hard for him.
words.ex_cn: 从学校到工作的转变对他来说很难。
words.en: The process or a period of changing from one state or condition to another.

words.ex: He crossed the threshold of adulthood at 18.
words.ex_cn: 他在18岁时进入了成年的起始点。
words.en: The threshold of something is the point at which it begins or changes.

words.tr:
adj. 被羞辱的
v. 使屈辱；使丢脸；使蒙羞；“humiliate”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He felt humiliated when he failed the test in front of everyone.
words.ex_cn: 当他当着大家的面考试失败时，他感到羞辱。
words.en: Feeling ashamed or foolish because you have been made to look weak, stupid, or ridiculous.

words.ex: The continuity of the story made it easy to follow.
words.ex_cn: 这个故事的连续性让它容易理解。
words.en: Continuity is the fact that something continues to happen or exist, with no great changes or interruptions.

words.ex: He does not want to intrude on their conversation.
words.ex_cn: 他不想插话他们的谈话。
words.en: To intrude means to enter somewhere or become involved in a situation where you are not wanted or are not supposed to be.

words.ex: He decisively chose the red shirt.
words.ex_cn: 他果断地选了红色的衬衫。
words.en: In a manner that settles an issue convincingly or produces a definite result.

words.tr:
adj. 令人安慰的
v. 安慰；“comfort”的现在分词
words.ex: The news was comforting to those who had been worried.
words.ex_cn: 这个消息对那些一直担心的人来说是一种安慰。
words.en: Making you feel less sad or worried; giving comfort.

words.ex: She polished the silverware before dinner.
words.ex_cn: 她在晚餐前擦拭了银器。
words.en: Silverware refers to items made of silver, especially tableware such as knives, forks, and spoons.

words.ex: The sailor fell overboard during the storm.
words.ex_cn: 水手在风暴中从船上掉入海中。
words.en: If someone falls overboard, they fall from a ship into the water. It can also mean doing something to an excessive degree.

words.tr:
n. 勒索；敲诈
v. 勒索；讹诈
words.ex: He threatened to tell the truth unless she paid him money — that's blackmail.
words.ex_cn: 他威胁说，除非她付钱，否则就说出真相——这就是敲诈。
words.en: Blackmail is the action of threatening to reveal a secret about someone, unless they do something you want, such as give you money.

words.tr: v. 体现；使具体化；包含
words.ex: He embodies kindness and patience.
words.ex_cn: 他体现了善良和耐心。
words.en: To embody means to represent a quality or an idea exactly; to include or contain something.

words.tr: adj. 愿意的；乐意的； v. “will”的现在分词；
words.ex: He is willing to help his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他愿意帮助他的朋友。
words.en: If someone is willing to do something, they are happy to do it if it is needed.

words.tr: adj. 自负的；骄傲自大的
words.ex: He is conceited because he thinks he is the smartest.
words.ex_cn: 他自以为是，因为他觉得自己最聪明。
words.en: If you say that someone is conceited, you are showing your disapproval of the fact that they are far too proud of their abilities or achievements.

words.tr: v. 摇动；“shake”的过去分词； adj. 受惊吓的；
words.ex: He was shaken by the strong wind.
words.ex_cn: 他被强风摇动了。
words.en: If you are shaken, you are upset and unable to think calmly because of something that has happened.

words.tr: adv. （用以询问大概的地方）在什么地方；
words.ex: I don't know his whereabouts.
words.ex_cn: 我不知道他在什么地方。
words.en: The place where someone or something is.

words.ex: The painting depicts a quiet village at sunset.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画描绘了一个宁静的村庄在日落时分的景象。
words.en: To depict someone or something means to show or represent them in a work of art such as a drawing or painting.

words.tr:
v. 害怕；畏惧
n. 恐惧；畏惧
words.ex: He dreads going to the dentist.
words.ex_cn: 他害怕去看牙医。
words.en: If you dread something, you fear it intensely.

words.ex: The teacher made an intervention to help the student.
words.ex_cn: 老师进行了干预以帮助学生。
words.en: Intervention is the act of intervening, especially in a situation to prevent something undesirable from happening.

words.ex: His perception of the sound was very sharp.
words.ex_cn: 他对声音的感知非常敏锐。
words.en: Your perception of something is the way that you think about it or the impression you have of it.

words.ex: He had a stumble on the rocky path.
words.ex_cn: 他在布满石头的小路上绊了一跤。
words.en: To stumble means to trip or momentarily lose one's balance while walking or running. It can also refer to speaking in a hesitant or faltering manner.

words.ex: He walks to the chapel every Sunday.
words.ex_cn: 他每个星期天都去小教堂。
words.en: A chapel is a small building or room used for Christian worship, typically one that is not a parish church.

words.ex: He was wary of strangers who offered free gifts.
words.ex_cn: 他对那些提供免费礼物的陌生人保持谨慎。
words.en: If you are wary of something or someone, you are cautious because you do not know much about them and you believe they may be dangerous or cause problems.

words.tr: adj. 有精神病的；心理不正常的；精神紊乱的； v. 打扰；妨碍；“disturb”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The disturbed man talked to himself all day.
words.ex_cn: 那个有精神病的人整天自言自语。
words.en: If someone is disturbed, they are very worried or troubled by something.

words.tr: phrase. 在某种程度上，就某种程度而言
words.ex: He will help you insofar as he can.
words.ex_cn: 他能帮多少就帮多少。
words.en: to the extent or degree that

words.ex: The village has a quaint old church.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄有一座古色古香的古老教堂。
words.en: Something that is quaint is attractive because it is unusual and old-fashioned.

words.tr: adj. 清醒的；严肃的；素淡的；
words.ex: He stayed sober after drinking only water.
words.ex_cn: 他只喝了水，保持清醒。
words.en: If you are sober, you are not drunk. If you are sober, you are serious and thoughtful.

words.tr: n. 军队；装甲部队；骑兵队；连队；童子军中队；军队( troop的名词复数 )；
words.ex: The troops marched into the city.
words.ex_cn: 军队进入了这座城市。
words.en: Troops are soldiers, especially when they are in a large organized group doing a particular task.

words.ex: He did it out of spite.
words.ex_cn: 他出于恶意做了这件事。
words.en: If you do something out of spite, you do it because you want to hurt or upset someone.

words.ex: The budget is a constraint on our project.
words.ex_cn: 预算是我们项目的限制。
words.en: A constraint is something that limits or controls what you can do.

words.ex: The earthquake was a catastrophe.
words.ex_cn: 这场地震是一场灾难。
words.en: An event causing great and often sudden damage or suffering; a disaster.

words.ex: Wearing a helmet is a preventive measure.
words.ex_cn: 戴头盔是一种预防性的措施。
words.en: Designed to stop something undesirable from occurring.

words.ex: The resolution of the conflict took many meetings.
words.ex_cn: 这个冲突的解决花了多次会议。
words.en: A resolution is a formal decision made at a meeting by the vote of the people who are there. It can also refer to a firm decision to do or not to do something.

words.ex: The procession moved slowly down the street.
words.ex_cn: 行列缓缓沿着街道行进。
words.en: A procession is a group of people who are walking, riding, or driving in a line as part of a public event.

words.ex: His intellect helps him solve difficult problems.
words.ex_cn: 他的智力帮助他解决难题。
words.en: The ability to understand and think in a logical way about things.

words.ex: He speculates that it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他推测明天会下雨。
words.en: If you speculate about something, you make guesses about its nature or identity, or about what might happen.

words.tr: adv. 无限期地；不确定地；
words.ex: The meeting was postponed indefinitely.
words.ex_cn: 会议被无限期推迟了。
words.en: If something will happen indefinitely, it will happen for an unlimited or unknown period of time.

words.tr: adj. 引起烦恼的；令人不安的； v. 打扰；妨碍；“disturb”的现在分词；
words.ex: The movie showed a disturbing scene of violence.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影展示了一个引起烦恼的暴力场景。
words.en: If you describe something as disturbing, you mean that it makes you feel anxious or upset.

words.ex: The children stood in awe at the sight of the mountains.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们看到山时感到敬畏。
words.en: A feeling of reverential respect mixed with fear or wonder.

words.tr: adv. 若有所思地；沉思地；意味深长地；体贴地；关心地；
words.ex: He sat thoughtfully by the window, staring at the rain.
words.ex_cn: 他若有所思地坐在窗边，凝视着雨。
words.en: In a way that shows careful consideration or attention.

words.tr: n. 不容忍；不容异己；偏狭
words.ex: He shows intolerance toward people who think differently.
words.ex_cn: 他对他人的不同想法表现出不容忍。
words.en: Intolerance is unwillingness to accept views, beliefs, or behavior that differ from one's own.

words.ex: The boys are playing dice after school.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们放学后玩掷骰游戏。
words.en: Small cubes marked on each side with spots numbering from one to six, used in games of chance; to cut food into small cubes.

words.ex: His conviction that honesty is important never changed.
words.ex_cn: 他坚信诚实很重要，从未改变。
words.en: A conviction is a strong belief or opinion, or the state of being found guilty of a crime in a court of law.

words.ex: He made a persistent effort to learn English.
words.ex_cn: 他持续努力学习英语。
words.en: Continuing firmly or obstinately in a course of action in spite of difficulty or opposition.

words.ex: He smiled at the recollection of his childhood.
words.ex_cn: 他回忆起童年时微笑了。
words.en: The act of remembering something or the ability to remember.

words.ex: The civilian population stayed safe during the conflict.
words.ex_cn: 平民在冲突期间保持安全。
words.en: A civilian is a person who is not a member of the military or of a police or firefighting force.

words.tr:
n. 婴儿；
adj. 初期的；
words.ex: The infant is sleeping in the crib.
words.ex_cn: 婴儿正在婴儿床里睡觉。
words.en: An infant is a baby or very young child.

words.tr:
n. 音高；球场；程度（最高点）；宣传论点；
v. 扎营；
words.ex: The singer changed the pitch of her voice.
words.ex_cn: 歌手改变了她声音的音高。
words.en: Pitch can refer to the highness or lowness of a sound, the act of throwing something, or a thick, black, sticky substance used for paving roads or waterproofing.

words.tr: n. 精神病学家；精神科医生
words.ex: He visits a psychiatrist every week.
words.ex_cn: 他每周去看一次精神科医生。
words.en: A psychiatrist is a medical doctor who specializes in the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of mental illnesses and emotional disorders.

words.tr: adj. 根本的；潜在的； v. “underlie”的现在分词；
words.ex: The underlying cause of the problem is poverty.
words.ex_cn: 这个问题的根本原因是贫困。
words.en: An underlying thing is the thing that is the most important or basic, although it is not easily noticed or stated directly.

words.tr:
n. 杂草；野草；
v. 除草；铲除；
words.ex: The garden is full of weeds.
words.ex_cn: 花园里长满了杂草。
words.en: A weed is a wild plant that grows in gardens or fields of crops and is not wanted because it harms the plants that are being grown.

words.tr:
n. 凝视；注视；
v. 凝视；注视；
words.ex: His gaze fixed on the sunset.
words.ex_cn: 他的凝视固定在日落上。
words.en: If you gaze at someone or something, you look steadily at them for a long time, for example because you find them attractive or interesting, or because you are thinking about something else.

words.tr: n. 严酷的考验；痛苦的经历；煎熬
words.ex: He went through a long ordeal before he found peace.
words.ex_cn: 他在找到平静之前经历了一段漫长的磨难。
words.en: An ordeal is a very unpleasant and prolonged experience.

words.ex: He is facing homelessness after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业后正面临无家可归。
words.en: The state of having no home or permanent place of residence.

words.ex: The government announced a major reform in education.
words.ex_cn: 政府宣布了教育方面的重大改革。
words.en: If someone reforms a system, they change or improve it.

words.ex: The country has an underdeveloped economy.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家经济不发达。
words.en: An underdeveloped country or region is one that is less developed economically and socially than most others, with many of its people living in poverty.

words.tr: n. 混乱；动荡；骚乱；恐慌
words.ex: The storm caused turmoil in the town.
words.ex_cn: 风暴给小镇带来了混乱。
words.en: A state of great disturbance, confusion, or uncertainty.

words.ex: The lake at dawn offers perfect tranquility.
words.ex_cn: 黎明时分的湖泊带来完全的宁静。
words.en: A state of peace and quiet.

words.ex: The scarcity of water caused problems in the village.
words.ex_cn: 水的缺乏给村庄带来了问题。
words.en: A scarcity of something is a situation in which there is not enough of it.

words.ex: The coldness of the water made him shiver.
words.ex_cn: 水的寒冷让他发抖。
words.en: The absence of heat or warmth; low temperature, or a lack of friendliness or enthusiasm.

words.tr: v. 有关；把…联系起来；认同；叙述；理解；
words.ex: This story relates to your childhood.
words.ex_cn: 这个故事与你的童年有关。
words.en: If you relate a story, you tell it. If two things relate, they are connected in some way.

words.ex: He used a disposable cup for his coffee.
words.ex_cn: 他用了一次性杯子喝咖啡。
words.en: Something that is disposable is intended to be thrown away after use.

words.ex: The family is in a difficult plight after losing their home.
words.ex_cn: 这家人在失去家园后陷入了困境。
words.en: A plight is a difficult or adverse situation, especially one that is hard to escape. It can also refer to a solemn promise or pledge.

words.tr: adj. 传染性的；有感染力的；
words.ex: The virus is infectious and spreads quickly.
words.ex_cn: 这种病毒具有传染性，传播迅速。
words.en: An infectious disease can be passed from one person to another, especially through the air they breathe.

words.ex: He was profoundly moved by the music.
words.ex_cn: 他被音乐深深打动了。
words.en: In a profound manner; deeply.

words.ex: The synonym of 'happy' is 'glad'.
words.ex_cn: ‘happy’的同义词是‘glad’。
words.en: A synonym is a word or phrase that means exactly or nearly the same as another word or phrase in the same language.

words.ex: He worked intensely to finish the project.
words.ex_cn: 他强烈地工作以完成这个项目。
words.en: If something is intense, it is very great or extreme in strength or degree.

words.ex: His knowledge of history is superficial.
words.ex_cn: 他对历史的了解是表面的。
words.en: If you describe someone as superficial, you disapprove of them because they do not think deeply, and have little understanding of anything serious or important.

words.tr: adj. 独自的；单独的；孤寂的；
words.ex: He lives in a solitary house far from the town.
words.ex_cn: 他住在离城镇很远的独自一人的房子里。
words.en: A solitary person or thing is the only one in a place.

words.tr: v. 花费；度过；“spend”的现在分词； n. 花费；开销；
words.ex: He is spending money on books.
words.ex_cn: 他正在花钱买书。
words.en: Spending refers to the act of using money to buy or pay for something.

words.ex: He gave her an abusive shout.
words.ex_cn: 他对她大喊大叫，态度虐待。
words.en: If someone is abusive, they use rude and insulting words or behave violently towards someone else.

words.tr: adj. 难以置信的；不可想象的；
words.ex: The damage from the storm was unimaginable.
words.ex_cn: 风暴造成的破坏难以置信。
words.en: If you describe something as unimaginable, you are emphasizing that it is difficult to imagine or understand because it is not part of people's normal experience.

words.tr: n. 公民投票；全民公决；
words.ex: The country held a referendum to decide on the new law.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家举行了公民投票来决定新法律。
words.en: A referendum is a direct vote in which an entire electorate is invited to vote on a particular proposal. This may result in the adoption of a new law.

words.ex: The bonus is an incentive to work harder.
words.ex_cn: 奖金是努力工作的动机。
words.en: Something that encourages a person to do something or to work harder.

words.tr: adj. 唯物论的；物质至上主义的
words.ex: He is materialistic and only cares about money.
words.ex_cn: 他是个唯物论者，只关心钱。
words.en: If you describe a person or society as materialistic, you are critical of them because they attach too much importance to money and material possessions.

words.tr: n. 额外费用；保险费；溢价；
words.ex: You need to pay a premium for faster delivery.
words.ex_cn: 你需要支付额外费用才能享受更快的配送。
words.en: A premium is an amount of money that you pay regularly to an insurance company for an insurance policy, or an amount of money that is more than usual for a product or service because it is of higher quality.

words.ex: His words are a contradiction.
words.ex_cn: 他的话是矛盾的。
words.en: A contradiction is a situation or statement in which two aspects or elements are opposed to each other, making it impossible for both to be true at the same time.

words.ex: The dog fell into a deep pit.
words.ex_cn: 狗掉进了一个深坑。
words.en: A pit is a large hole in the ground, either natural or as a result of digging. It can also refer to a hollow or indentation in a surface, or a place where something is extracted, such as a mine. As a verb, to pit means to set someone or something in competition or to make a hollow or indentation in a surface.

words.ex: He was born in the province of Guangdong.
words.ex_cn: 他出生在广东省。
words.en: A province is a large area of a country that has its own administration and often its own culture.

words.ex: He went back to retrieve his keys.
words.ex_cn: 他回去取回他的钥匙。
words.en: To retrieve something means to get it back from somewhere, especially after it has been lost or taken away.

words.ex: He shows self-discipline by waking up early every day.
words.ex_cn: 他通过每天早起展现自律。
words.en: The ability to control yourself and to make yourself work hard or behave in a particular way without needing anyone else to tell you what to do.

words.ex: The farmer drives a tractor in the field.
words.ex_cn: 农夫在田里开拖拉机。
words.en: A tractor is a powerful motor vehicle with large rear wheels, used chiefly on farms for hauling equipment and trailers.

words.ex: The necklace is an imitation made of plastic.
words.ex_cn: 这条项链是用塑料做的仿制品。
words.en: An imitation of something is a copy of it.

words.tr: adj. （言行）谨慎的；不显眼的；朴素的
words.ex: He was discreet about his personal life.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己的私生活很低调。
words.en: If you are discreet, you are polite and careful in what you do or say, because you want to avoid embarrassing or offending someone.

words.ex: The implementation of the new rule took one month.
words.ex_cn: 新规则的履行花了一个月。
words.en: The act of putting a decision or plan into effect; execution.

words.ex: The child received vaccination last week.
words.ex_cn: 孩子上周接种了疫苗。
words.en: The act of introducing a vaccine into the body to produce immunity to a specific disease.

words.tr: n. 自立；依靠自己；自力更生
words.ex: He learns self-reliance from living alone.
words.ex_cn: 他通过独自生活学会自立。
words.en: Self-reliance is the ability to do things and make decisions by yourself, without needing other people to help you.

words.ex: Climbing the mountain without oxygen was a great feat.
words.ex_cn: 在不吸氧的情况下爬山是一项伟大的壮举。
words.en: A feat is an act or achievement that shows great courage, skill, or strength.

words.tr: n. 认可；识别；认识；承认；
words.ex: His hard work got recognition from his boss.
words.ex_cn: 他的努力得到了老板的认可。
words.en: The action or process of recognizing or being recognized, in particular.

words.ex: She was frantic to catch the last bus.
words.ex_cn: 她急忙赶着赶最后一班公交车。
words.en: If someone is frantic, they are behaving in a wild and desperate way, often because they are frightened or worried.

words.ex: He worked hard to fulfill his dream.
words.ex_cn: 他努力工作以实现自己的梦想。
words.en: To fulfill a task, role, or function means to do or perform it as required or expected.

words.tr:
adj. 精瘦的；精简的；不景气的；
v. 倾斜；倚靠；
words.ex: The dog is lean and fast.
words.ex_cn: 这只狗精瘦而敏捷。
words.en: If you lean in a particular direction, you bend your body in that direction. If you lean on or against someone or something, you rest against them so that they partly support your weight. If you describe someone as lean, you mean that they are thin but look strong and healthy. If you describe a period of time as lean, you mean that it is a time when people have very little of something, especially money.

words.ex: Reading books is his favorite pastime.
words.ex_cn: 读书是他最喜欢的消遣。
words.en: A pastime is something that you do because you enjoy it or are interested in it, rather than as a job.

words.tr: adj. 强有力的；有说服力的
words.ex: He gave a forceful speech to convince the crowd.
words.ex_cn: 他发表了一番有力的演讲来说服人群。
words.en: A forceful person expresses their opinions and wishes strongly, and people are easily persuaded by them.

words.tr:
n. 提倡者；
v. 提倡；
words.ex: He is an advocate for clean water.
words.ex_cn: 他是清洁用水的提倡者。
words.en: If you advocate a particular action or plan, you recommend it publicly.

words.ex: The boy showed toughness when he kept running despite the pain.
words.ex_cn: 尽管疼痛，这个男孩仍然坚持跑步，展现了坚韧。
words.en: The quality of being strong and not easily broken or damaged.

words.ex: The North Pole is covered with ice all year round.
words.ex_cn: 北极全年都被冰雪覆盖。
words.en: A pole is a long, thin, rounded piece of wood or metal, used especially for supporting things.

words.ex: His stubbornness made it hard to change his mind.
words.ex_cn: 他的固执使他难以改变主意。
words.en: The quality of being determined not to change your attitude or position on something, especially in spite of good arguments or reasons to do so.

words.ex: He exclaim when he saw the surprise.
words.ex_cn: 当他看到惊喜时，他大喊起来。
words.en: If you exclaim, you say something suddenly and loudly, often because you are surprised, excited, or angry.

words.tr:
n. 流体；流质；
adj. 流动的；
words.ex: Water is a common fluid.
words.ex_cn: 水是一种常见的流体。
words.en: A fluid is a substance that can flow and change its shape easily, such as a liquid or a gas.

words.tr:
n. 快照；
v. 突然断裂；猛然咬；
adj. 突然的；匆忙的；
words.ex: He took a snap of the sunset.
words.ex_cn: 他拍了一张日落的快照。
words.en: If something snaps or if you snap it, it breaks suddenly, usually with a sharp cracking noise. | A snap is a photograph. | If someone snaps, or if something snaps inside them, they suddenly stop being calm and become very angry.

words.ex: He has an obsessive need to clean everything.
words.ex_cn: 他有一种强迫性的需求，要把一切都打扫干净。
words.en: If someone's behaviour is obsessive, they cannot stop doing a particular thing or behaving in a particular way.

words.ex: The fearless girl climbed the tall tree.
words.ex_cn: 这个无畏的女孩爬上了高高的树。
words.en: If someone is fearless, they are not afraid of anything.

words.ex: The accident left him with a serious trauma on his leg.
words.ex_cn: 这场事故使他的腿受了严重的伤。
words.en: A trauma is a very distressing or disturbing experience.

words.ex: He had diarrhea after eating bad food.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了坏食物后得了腹泻。
words.en: A condition in which feces are discharged from the bowels frequently and in a liquid form.

words.ex: The validity of the test results is important.
words.ex_cn: 测试结果的有效性很重要。
words.en: The quality of being logically or factually sound; soundness or cogency.

words.ex: They plant trees to commemorate the fallen soldiers.
words.ex_cn: 他们种树以纪念阵亡的士兵。
words.en: To commemorate an important event or person means to remember them by means of a special action, ceremony, or specially created object.

words.ex: He follows a systematic approach to solve math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他用一种系统的方法来解决数学问题。
words.en: A systematic approach or method is one that is done according to a fixed plan, in a thorough and efficient way.

words.ex: This experiment is a paradigm of scientific method.
words.ex_cn: 这个实验是科学方法的范例。
words.en: A paradigm is a model or pattern that is considered to be a typical example of something.

words.ex: The family reduced their monthly expenditure.
words.ex_cn: 这个家庭减少了每月的开支。
words.en: Expenditure is the spending of money on something, or the money that is spent on something.

words.tr:
v. 把…归因于；由…引起；
n. 品质；属性；特征；属性；
words.ex: He attributes his success to hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他把他的成功归因于努力工作。
words.en: If you attribute something to an event or situation, you think that it was caused by that event or situation.

words.ex: He felt insecurity when he lost his job.
words.ex_cn: 当他失去工作时，他感到不安全感。
words.en: Insecurity is a feeling of uncertainty or anxiety about oneself or one's situation.

words.ex: His quest for truth led him to travel the world.
words.ex_cn: 他对真理的探求使他环游世界。
words.en: A quest is a long or difficult search for something.

words.ex: The man was punished for fraud.
words.ex_cn: 这个人因欺骗而受到惩罚。
words.en: Fraud is the crime of gaining money or financial benefits by a trick or by lying.

words.ex: The soup was too bland for me.
words.ex_cn: 这汤太淡了，我不喜欢。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as bland, you mean that they are rather dull and unexciting.

words.tr: adj. 可触摸的；实际的；有形的；确凿的；
words.ex: The statue is tangible and can be touched.
words.ex_cn: 这座雕像可以触摸，是实实在在的。
words.en: Something that is tangible is clear enough or definite enough to be easily seen, felt, or noticed.

words.ex: He wields his knowledge to solve problems.
words.ex_cn: 他运用自己的知识来解决问题。
words.en: To wield something means to hold and use it, especially as a weapon or tool. It can also mean to have and be able to use power or influence.

words.tr: adj. 脆弱的；易碎的；不牢固的；
words.ex: The glass is fragile and might break easily.
words.ex_cn: 这个玻璃很脆弱，容易碎。
words.en: If something is fragile, it is easily broken or damaged.

words.ex: He got a blister on his foot from new shoes.
words.ex_cn: 他新鞋磨出了一个水泡。
words.en: A blister is a small pocket of fluid within the upper layers of the skin, typically caused by forceful rubbing, burning, freezing, chemical exposure or infection. As a verb, it means to form such a pocket of fluid.

words.ex: He has an inclination to help others.
words.ex_cn: 他有帮助他人的倾向。
words.en: An inclination is a feeling that makes you want to act in a particular way, or a tendency to do something.

words.tr:
n. 指关节
v. 用指关节…；屈从
words.ex: He cracked his knuckles before the game.
words.ex_cn: 他在比赛前掰响了指关节。
words.en: The knuckles are the joints of the fingers, especially where they join the hand.

words.tr: n. 假定；推定；冒昧；放肆
words.ex: His presumption that he would win surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他以为自己会赢的这种假设让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: A presumption is something that is thought to be true because it is likely, although there is no proof.

words.ex: The movie was mediocre and not worth watching.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影很平庸，不值得看。
words.en: If you describe something as mediocre, you mean that it is of average quality but you think it should be better.

words.tr: adv. 不可避免地；不得已地
words.ex: He will unavoidably miss the bus if he doesn't leave now.
words.ex_cn: 如果他现在不走，就不可避免地会错过公交车。
words.en: in a way that cannot be avoided; necessarily

words.tr: adj. 多方面的；有多种技能的；
words.ex: He is a versatile player who can play many positions.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名多方面的运动员，能打多个位置。
words.en: Able to adapt or be adapted to many different functions or activities.

words.ex: He staggered home after drinking too much.
words.ex_cn: 他喝多了后摇摇晃晃地走回家。
words.en: If you stagger, you walk very unsteadily, as if you are about to fall.

words.ex: His silence was an implicit apology.
words.ex_cn: 他的沉默是一种含蓄的道歉。
words.en: Something that is implicit is expressed in an indirect way.

words.tr:
v. 给…打钩；发出滴嗒声；
n. 钩号；
words.ex: Please tick the box if you agree.
words.ex_cn: 如果你同意，请在方框里打钩。
words.en: The word 'tick' can refer to the sound a clock makes, a very short period of time, a mark used to indicate something, or a type of small insect. As a verb, it can mean to make a ticking sound or to mark something with a tick.

words.ex: The floppy ears of the dog waved when it ran.
words.ex_cn: 狗的松垂耳朵在它跑时晃动。
words.en: Something that is floppy is loose and soft, often hanging or bending in a way that suggests it lacks stiffness.

words.ex: He uses contraception to avoid having a baby.
words.ex_cn: 他使用避孕措施来避免怀孕。
words.en: Contraception is the use of methods or devices to prevent pregnancy.

words.ex: The people showed resistance against the unfair law.
words.ex_cn: 人们对这项不公平的法律表示抵抗。
words.en: Resistance is the refusal to accept or comply with something; the attempt to prevent something by action or argument.

words.ex: His surname is Smith.
words.ex_cn: 他的姓是史密斯。
words.en: Your surname is the name that you share with other members of your family. In English-speaking countries and many other countries, it is your last name.

words.ex: The company follows ethical practices in hiring.
words.ex_cn: 该公司在招聘中遵循伦理规范。
words.en: Relating to moral principles or the branch of knowledge dealing with these.

words.tr:
n. 意图；目的；
adj. 专注的；
words.ex: His intent was to help, not to hurt.
words.ex_cn: 他的意图是帮助，而不是伤害。
words.en: If you are intent on doing something, you are determined to get it done. If you have an intent to do something, you have a plan or purpose in mind.

words.ex: The story has good coherence, so it is easy to understand.
words.ex_cn: 这个故事很有连贯性，所以很容易理解。
words.en: Coherence is the quality of being logical and consistent.

words.tr:
v. 防止；战斗；抑制；
n. 战斗；
words.ex: The new law aims to combat pollution.
words.ex_cn: 这项新法律旨在防止污染。
words.en: Combat refers to fighting, especially during a war. It can also mean to try to stop something harmful from happening or increasing.

words.ex: Theoretically, the plan should work.
words.ex_cn: 理论上，这个计划应该可行。
words.en: In a way that relates to the theory of a subject or area of study rather than its practical application.

words.ex: He fundamentally disagrees with the policy.
words.ex_cn: 他根本上不同意这项政策。
words.en: In a basic and important way; essentially.

words.ex: The intrusion of strangers made her feel unsafe.
words.ex_cn: 陌生人的闯入让她感到不安全。
words.en: An intrusion is an unwanted event or person in a situation where they are not welcome or do not belong.

words.tr:
n. 叙述；叙事；
adj. 叙述性的；
words.ex: He told a simple narrative about his childhood.
words.ex_cn: 他讲了一个关于他童年的简单故事。
words.en: A narrative is a story or an account of a series of events.

words.tr: adv. 无限地；无穷地；极大地；
words.ex: The stars are infinitely far away.
words.ex_cn: 星星离得无限远。
words.en: In a way that is without limits or bounds; extremely or immeasurably.

words.tr: n. 咨询服务； v. “counsel”的现在分词；
words.ex: He went to school counseling for help with stress.
words.ex_cn: 他去学校咨询服务中心寻求减压帮助。
words.en: Counseling is the process of helping someone to deal with and understand their problems by listening to them and giving them advice.

words.ex: He gave a philosophical answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了一个哲学性的回答。
words.en: Relating to or based on philosophy; calm and thoughtful in the face of problems.

words.ex: The painting is a beautiful representation of nature.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画是对自然的美丽表现。
words.en: A representation of something is a picture, a model of it, or a description of it that you create or that someone else creates for you.

words.ex: The dove is a symbolic bird of peace.
words.ex_cn: 鸽子是和平的象征性鸟类。
words.en: If you describe an event, action, or procedure as symbolic, you mean that it represents an important change, although it has little practical effect.

words.ex: He must confront his fears.
words.ex_cn: 他必须面对自己的恐惧。
words.en: If you confront a difficult situation or issue, you accept the fact that it exists and try to deal with it.

words.tr:
adj. 僻静的；隐僻的； 退隐的
v. 隔离；隔绝；隐居；“seclude”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The cabin is secluded in the woods.
words.ex_cn: 小木屋坐落在树林中，十分僻静。
words.en: A secluded place is quiet, private, and not near people or things that disturb you.

words.ex: The earthquake caused total devastation in the city.
words.ex_cn: 地震给这座城市造成了严重的破坏。
words.en: The state of being devastated; severe and widespread destruction or damage.

words.tr: adj. 漆黑的; 黑洞洞; 黑咕隆咚; 黑漆漆
words.ex: The room was pitch-dark after the power went out.
words.ex_cn: 停电后，房间一片漆黑。
words.en: If a place is pitch-dark, it is completely dark.

words.ex: He was courteous to everyone he met.
words.ex_cn: 他对遇到的每个人都很有礼貌。
words.en: Someone who is courteous is polite and respectful to other people.

words.tr: adj. 可疑的；有问题的；不可靠的；
words.ex: The deal seemed questionable.
words.ex_cn: 这笔交易看起来可疑。
words.en: If you say that something is questionable, you mean that it is not obviously true or real, and therefore possibly not valid or reliable.

words.ex: The bright light was a stimulus for the baby to open his eyes.
words.ex_cn: 明亮的光线是让婴儿睁开眼睛的刺激物。
words.en: Something that causes growth or activity.

words.ex: The company improved data retention after upgrading its system.
words.ex_cn: 公司在升级系统后提高了数据保留能力。
words.en: The action of retaining something; the continued possession, use, or control of something.

words.tr:
n. 低语声；嘟哝
v. 低语；咕哝；私下抱怨
words.ex: I heard a murmur from the next room.
words.ex_cn: 我听到隔壁房间传来低语声。
words.en: A murmur is a low, indistinct, continuous sound, as of a stream or of voices.

words.tr: adj. 爱管闲事的；爱打听的
words.ex: The nosy neighbor always asks too many questions.
words.ex_cn: 那个爱管闲事的邻居总是问太多问题。
words.en: If you describe someone as nosy, you mean that they are too interested in things that do not concern them, especially other people's affairs.

words.tr: adj. 精美的；细腻的；强烈的
words.ex: She wore an exquisite dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一条精美的裙子去参加派对。
words.en: Something that is exquisite is extremely beautiful or pleasant, especially in a delicate or refined way.

words.ex: The goal is attainable if you work hard.
words.ex_cn: 如果你努力工作，这个目标是可以达到的。
words.en: If something is attainable, it is possible to achieve it.

words.tr: adj. 暂时的；临时的；期间的；
words.ex: He is the interim manager until a new one is hired.
words.ex_cn: 在招聘到新的经理之前，他是临时经理。
words.en: An interim is a period of time between one event, process, or period and another, especially one of temporary nature.

words.ex: He squandered all his money on games.
words.ex_cn: 他把所有的钱都浪费在游戏上了。
words.en: If you squander money, resources, or opportunities, you waste them in a foolish or careless way.

words.ex: He found a way whereby he could save money.
words.ex_cn: 他找到了一种借以省钱的方法。
words.en: You use whereby to introduce a clause in which you mention the means by which something happens.

words.ex: The village suffered from famine last year.
words.ex_cn: 去年这个村庄遭受了饥荒。
words.en: A famine is a serious shortage of food in a country, which may cause many people to get sick or die.

words.ex: The universe may be infinite.
words.ex_cn: 宇宙可能是无限的。
words.en: If you describe something as infinite, you are emphasizing that it is extremely great in amount or degree.

words.ex: He made an unscrupulous deal to save money.
words.ex_cn: 他为了省钱做了不道德的交易。
words.en: If you describe someone as unscrupulous, you are critical of them because they are prepared to act in a dishonest or immoral way in order to get what they want.

words.ex: The resilient child bounced back quickly after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 这个适应力强的孩子在事故后很快恢复了。
words.en: Something that is resilient is strong and not easily damaged by being hit, stretched, or squeezed.

words.tr:
n. 流动；
v. 漂移；
words.ex: The drift of the river carries leaves downstream.
words.ex_cn: 河流的流动将树叶冲向下游。
words.en: If something or someone drifts somewhere, they move there slowly or gradually. As a noun, drift can refer to a slow, gradual movement or change, or the general meaning or intent of something.

words.tr:
v. 呻吟；叹息
n. 呻吟声；叹息声
words.ex: He groaned when he saw the heavy box.
words.ex_cn: 他看到那个沉重的箱子时呻吟了一声。
words.en: If you groan, you make a long, low sound because you are in pain, or because you are upset or unhappy about something.

words.ex: The motion of the ball is very fast.
words.ex_cn: 球的运动非常快。
words.en: The action or process of moving or being moved.

words.tr: n. 内向的人；不喜欢与人交往的人
words.ex: He is an introvert who likes reading alone.
words.ex_cn: 他是个喜欢独自读书的内向者。
words.en: An introvert is a person who tends to shrink from social contacts and to become preoccupied with their own thoughts.

words.ex: The fish swim among the coral in the sea.
words.ex_cn: 鱼在海中的珊瑚间游动。
words.en: A hard stony substance secreted by certain marine coelenterates as an external skeleton, typically forming large reefs in warm seas.

words.ex: The faraway village is hard to reach.
words.ex_cn: 那个遥远的村庄很难到达。
words.en: A faraway place is a long distance away from where you are.

words.ex: The evidence is indisputable.
words.ex_cn: 证据是无可争辩的。
words.en: Something that is indisputable is true and cannot be denied or questioned.

words.tr: adj. 边缘的；页边的；微不足道的；不重要的
words.ex: The village is on the marginal area of the city.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄位于城市的边缘地区。
words.en: If you describe something as marginal, you mean that it is small or not very important.

words.tr: adj. 不忠的；背叛的；不忠诚的
words.ex: He was disloyal to his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他对朋友不忠。
words.en: If someone is disloyal, they are not loyal to a person, organization, or idea that they are supposed to support.

words.ex: His impatience made him shout at the waiter.
words.ex_cn: 他的不耐烦让他对服务员大喊。
words.en: Impatience is the feeling of being annoyed by someone's mistakes or because you have to wait.

words.ex: He filed a lawsuit against the company.
words.ex_cn: 他向这家公司提起了诉讼。
words.en: A lawsuit is a case in a court of law which concerns a dispute between two people or organizations.

words.ex: The judge made an unbalanced decision.
words.ex_cn: 法官做出了一个不公正的决定。
words.en: If you describe someone as unbalanced, you mean that they appear disturbed and upset or they seem to be slightly mad.

words.tr:
n. 回声；
v. 回响；
words.ex: The echo came back from the mountain.
words.ex_cn: 回声从山上反弹回来。
words.en: An echo is a sound which is caused by a noise being reflected off a surface such as a wall.

words.ex: He wants to be self-sufficient by growing his own food.
words.ex_cn: 他想通过自己种食物来实现自给自足。
words.en: A self-sufficient person or thing is able to provide for themselves without outside assistance.

words.ex: The country faced unrest after the election.
words.ex_cn: 选举后，这个国家陷入了动荡。
words.en: A state of dissatisfaction, disturbance, and agitation, typically involving public demonstrations or disorder.

words.ex: He listened to his conscience and told the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他听从了良心，说出了真相。
words.en: Your conscience is the part of your mind that tells you whether what you are doing is right or wrong.

words.tr:
n. 火花；火星；
v. 激发；
words.ex: The match produced a small spark.
words.ex_cn: 火柴产生了一个小火花。
words.en: A spark is a small fiery particle thrown off from a fire, alight in ashes, or produced by striking together two hard surfaces such as stone or metal.

words.ex: He hums a tune while walking.
words.ex_cn: 他走路时哼着曲子。
words.en: To make a low, steady, continuous sound like that of a bee.

words.ex: He is an industrious student who studies every day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个勤勉的学生，每天都学习。
words.en: Someone who is industrious works hard and is determined.

words.tr: adj. 增补性的；补充性的；
words.ex: The teacher gave supplementary notes for the lesson.
words.ex_cn: 老师为这节课提供了增补性的笔记。
words.en: Supplementary things are added to something in order to improve it or make it more complete.

words.ex: The child showed signs of talent in infancy.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子在婴儿期就表现出天赋。
words.en: The earliest period of childhood, especially before the ability to walk has been acquired.

words.ex: The mortality rate in the region increased last year.
words.ex_cn: 去年该地区的死亡率上升了。
words.en: Mortality refers to the state of being subject to death or the number of deaths in a particular population or period.

words.tr: adj. 有缺点的；有缺陷的；有毛病的；
words.ex: The defective phone wouldn't turn on.
words.ex_cn: 这部有缺点的手机无法开机。
words.en: If something is defective, there is something wrong with it and it does not work properly.

words.ex: He sneezed and air came out of his nostril.
words.ex_cn: 他打了个喷嚏，空气从他的鼻孔里出来。
words.en: Either of the two external openings of the nose, which allow air to enter the lungs and smells to be detected.

words.tr:
v. 拖；拉；拖运；
n. 拖；拉；拖运；
words.ex: He hauled the heavy box across the room.
words.ex_cn: 他把沉重的箱子拖过了房间。
words.en: To haul something means to pull it or carry it with a lot of effort.

words.ex: He made a plea for help.
words.ex_cn: 他恳求帮助。
words.en: A plea is a request or an appeal made in an urgent or emotional manner, or a statement made by someone in a court of law in which they say whether they are guilty of a crime or not.

words.tr: n. 道德规范；伦理标准；
words.ex: The company follows a strong ethic of honesty.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司遵循诚实的道德规范。
words.en: An ethic is a moral principle or set of moral principles that guides the behavior of a person or group, especially in a professional context.

words.tr: n. 推理；推论； v. “reason”的现在分词；
words.ex: His reasoning helped solve the puzzle.
words.ex_cn: 他的推理帮助解决了这个谜题。
words.en: the process of thinking about something in a logical way in order to form a conclusion or judgment

words.ex: His perseverance helped him finish the marathon.
words.ex_cn: 他的毅力帮助他完成了马拉松。
words.en: Perseverance is the quality of continuing to try to achieve a particular aim despite difficulties.

words.tr:
v. 喘气；喘息；倒抽气
n. 喘气；喘息
words.ex: He gasped when he saw the big snake.
words.ex_cn: 当他看到那条大蛇时，他倒吸了一口冷气。
words.en: To take a short, quick breath through the mouth, especially because of surprise, pain, or shock.

words.ex: The police investigated the assault on the old man.
words.ex_cn: 警方调查了对那位老人的攻击。
words.en: An assault is a physical attack on someone, or a military attack on a place.

words.ex: He is studying constitutional law at university.
words.ex_cn: 他正在大学学习宪法。
words.en: Relating to the constitution of a country or organization; in accordance with a political constitution.

words.tr: adj. 充满烟的；冒烟的；烟状的；有烟味的；
words.ex: The room was smoky after the fire.
words.ex_cn: 火灾后，房间里充满了烟。
words.en: If a place is smoky, it is full of smoke or has a lot of smoke in it.

words.tr: v. 考虑；深思；凝视；思考…的可能性
words.ex: He contemplates quitting his job.
words.ex_cn: 他正在考虑辞去工作。
words.en: If you contemplate an action, you think about whether to do it or not.

words.ex: He remained unaffected by the noise.
words.ex_cn: 他没有受到噪音的影响。
words.en: If someone or something is unaffected by an event or occurrence, they are not changed by it in any way.

words.ex: There was clear hostility between the two neighbors.
words.ex_cn: 两个邻居之间明显存在敌意。
words.en: Hostility is unfriendly or aggressive behaviour towards people or ideas.

words.ex: The island is uninhabited.
words.ex_cn: 这个岛没有人居住。
words.en: If a place is uninhabited, no people live there.

words.ex: I loathe waking up early.
words.ex_cn: 我讨厌早起。
words.en: If you loathe something or someone, you dislike them very much.

words.ex: The taxpayer paid his taxes on time.
words.ex_cn: 纳税人按时缴税了。
words.en: A taxpayer is a person or organization that pays taxes to the government.

words.ex: His words were contradictory.
words.ex_cn: 他的话是矛盾的。
words.en: If two or more facts, ideas, or statements are contradictory, they state or imply that opposite things are true.

words.tr: phrase. 可用收益；可支配收入；税后收入
words.ex: He uses his disposable income to buy books.
words.ex_cn: 他用可支配收入买书。
words.en: Disposable income is the amount of money that households have available for spending and saving after income taxes have been accounted for.

words.tr:
adj. 狂热入迷的；盲信的
n. 狂热者；盲信者
words.ex: He is a fanatic fan of soccer.
words.ex_cn: 他对足球狂热入迷。
words.en: A fanatic is a person who is very enthusiastic about and devoted to a particular activity, cause, or belief, often to an extreme degree.

words.tr:
v. 定罪；宣判有罪
n. 罪犯；囚犯
words.ex: The court convicted him of theft.
words.ex_cn: 法院判定他犯有盗窃罪。
words.en: If someone is convicted of a crime, they are found guilty of that crime in a court of law.

words.ex: He drinks decaffeinated coffee every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上喝无咖啡因咖啡。
words.en: Having had the caffeine removed.

words.tr:
n. 轻拍；
v. 轻拍；
words.ex: He gave the dog a gentle pat on the head.
words.ex_cn: 他轻轻拍了拍狗的头。
words.en: To gently touch someone or something with your hand flat.

words.ex: Dust particles float in the air.
words.ex_cn: 灰尘微粒漂浮在空气中。
words.en: A particle is a very small piece or amount of something.

words.ex: He took his words in a literal sense.
words.ex_cn: 他把他的话按字面意思理解。
words.en: If you describe something as the literal truth or a literal fact, you are emphasizing that it is true.

words.ex: The mother won custody of her child.
words.ex_cn: 母亲获得了孩子的监护权。
words.en: Custody is the legal right or duty to care for someone or something, especially a child after its parents have separated or died.

words.tr: adj. 正在进行中的；航行中的；
words.ex: The project is underway.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目正在进行中。
words.en: If something is underway, it is happening now.

words.ex: The teacher showed a specimen of a butterfly.
words.ex_cn: 老师展示了一个蝴蝶标本。
words.en: A specimen is a single thing or example of something, especially one that is used to represent the whole group or type.

words.tr: adj. 观察力敏锐的；谨慎遵守的；
words.ex: She is observant and notices small details.
words.ex_cn: 她观察力敏锐，能注意到细小的细节。
words.en: Someone who is observant pays close attention to things and notices more about them than most people do.

words.ex: A pocket calculator is handy for math problems.
words.ex_cn: 便携式计算器对于数学问题很方便。
words.en: If something is handy, it is useful and easy to use or to reach.

words.ex: The farmer stores hay in the barn.
words.ex_cn: 农夫把干草存放在谷仓里。
words.en: A barn is a large building on a farm in which crops or animals are kept.

words.ex: The bridge has a strong structural design.
words.ex_cn: 这座桥有坚固的结构设计。
words.en: Relating to the arrangement of and relations between the parts or elements of something complex.

words.ex: She baked a chicken casserole for dinner.
words.ex_cn: 她为晚餐烤了一道鸡肉砂锅菜。
words.en: A casserole is a dish consisting of a mixture of foods baked together in the oven.

words.ex: The two countries formed an alliance to fight the enemy.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家结成联盟以对抗敌人。
words.en: An alliance is a group of countries or political parties that are formally united and working together because they have similar aims.

words.ex: The rain precedes the storm.
words.ex_cn: 雨先于风暴来临。
words.en: If one event or period of time precedes another, it happens before it.

words.tr:
v. 皱眉；蹙额
n. 皱眉；蹙额
words.ex: He frowns when he hears bad news.
words.ex_cn: 他听到坏消息时会皱眉。
words.en: If you frown, you bring your eyebrows together so that there are lines on your face above your eyes, often because you are annoyed or worried.

words.ex: He is confined to his room because he is sick.
words.ex_cn: 他因为生病被限制在房间里。
words.en: If you confine something or someone, you limit them to a particular place or situation.

words.ex: It is an impossibility to finish this in one hour.
words.ex_cn: 在一个小时内完成这是不可能的。
words.en: If you refer to the impossibility of something, you mean that it is impossible.

words.tr: n. （宗教等的）仪式；例行习惯；
words.ex: The village holds a ritual every spring to pray for good weather.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄每年春天都举行一个仪式，祈求好天气。
words.en: A ritual is a religious service or other ceremony which involves a series of actions performed in a fixed order.

words.ex: He refused to accept mediocrity in his work.
words.ex_cn: 他拒绝在工作中接受平凡。
words.en: If you refer to the mediocrity of something, you mean that it is of average quality but you think it should be better.

words.tr: adj. 近视的；目光短浅的
words.ex: He is short-sighted and needs glasses to see far.
words.ex_cn: 他近视，需要戴眼镜才能看远。
words.en: If someone is short-sighted, they cannot see things clearly that are far away, or they do not plan for the future in a sensible way.

words.tr:
adj. 暗淡的；昏暗的；模糊的
v. （使）变暗淡；（使）变模糊；（使）减弱
words.ex: The room is dim because the lights are off.
words.ex_cn: 房间很暗，因为灯关了。
words.en: If a light or a place is dim, it is not bright or is not lit very strongly.

words.tr: adj. 老一套的；刻板的；带有成见的
words.ex: He wears stereotypical clothes for his job.
words.ex_cn: 他穿着符合刻板印象的职业服装。
words.en: A stereotypical idea of a type of person or thing is a fixed general idea that a lot of people have about it, which may be untrue in many cases.

words.ex: He owns five acres of farmland.
words.ex_cn: 他拥有五英亩的农田。
words.en: A unit of area used in the US Customary and the British Imperial systems, equal to 4,840 square yards or 4,046.86 square meters.

words.ex: Sleep is vitally important for health.
words.ex_cn: 睡眠对健康极其重要。
words.en: Vitally means in a way that is extremely important or necessary.

words.tr:
n. 小块；碎片；废金属；吵架
v. 废弃；取消
adj. 废弃的
words.ex: He picked up a scrap of paper from the floor.
words.ex_cn: 他从地上捡起一张纸片。
words.en: A scrap is a small piece or amount of something, especially one that is left over after the greater part has been used. It can also mean to discard or get rid of something as being no longer useful or necessary.

words.tr: n. 支持； v. 支持；“back”的现在分词；
words.ex: His backing helped the team win the match.
words.ex_cn: 他的支持帮助球队赢得了比赛。
words.en: Support or help.

words.ex: Birds inhabit the forest near the lake.
words.ex_cn: 鸟类居住在湖边的森林里。
words.en: If a place or region is inhabited by a group of people or a species of animal, those people or animals live there.

words.tr: adv. 外交上；用外交手腕
words.ex: He spoke diplomatically to avoid conflict.
words.ex_cn: 他说话很委婉，以避免冲突。
words.en: In a way that is related to diplomacy or tactful in dealing with others.

words.tr: v. 使增加至最大限度；最大化；
words.ex: He tries to maximize his profit by selling more.
words.ex_cn: 他通过多卖东西来使利润达到最大。
words.en: To maximize something means to make it as great in amount, size, or importance as possible.

words.ex: She wrote a poetic letter to her friend.
words.ex_cn: 她给朋友写了一封诗意的信。
words.en: Something that is poetic is very beautiful and expresses emotions in a sensitive or moving way.

words.tr: n. 长期存在的；持续相当长时间的；上演很长时间的
words.ex: This is a long-running TV show.
words.ex_cn: 这是一档长期存在的电视节目。
words.en: Something that is long-running has been happening or existing for a long time.

words.ex: He showed xenophobia toward people from other countries.
words.ex_cn: 他对来自其他国家的人表现出恐外心理。
words.en: Xenophobia is a strong feeling of dislike or fear of people from other countries.

words.ex: The ship carries a large cargo of rice.
words.ex_cn: 这艘船运载了大量大米货物。
words.en: Cargo refers to the goods carried by a ship, aircraft, or other large vehicle.

words.ex: The kitchen is hygienic and clean.
words.ex_cn: 厨房卫生且干净。
words.en: Something that is hygienic is clean and unlikely to cause illness.

words.tr:
adj. 不锋利的；耿直的
v. 使变钝
words.ex: The knife is blunt and cannot cut paper.
words.ex_cn: 这把刀不锋利，切不动纸。
words.en: If you are blunt, you say exactly what you think without trying to be polite.

words.ex: She tries to juggle her job and caring for her kids.
words.ex_cn: 她努力兼顾工作和照顾孩子。
words.en: If you juggle, you keep several objects in motion in the air at the same time by repeatedly throwing and catching them. Juggle can also mean to deal with several things at the same time, often in a skillful way.

words.ex: He sits by the fireplace in winter.
words.ex_cn: 冬天他坐在壁炉旁。
words.en: A fireplace is a place built into a wall where you can have a fire, especially in a house.

words.tr: v. 使粉碎；使破碎；使破灭；“shatter”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The stone shattered when it hit the ground.
words.ex_cn: 石头撞到地面时碎裂了。
words.en: If something is shattered, it is broken into many small pieces, or it is extremely tired or shocked.

words.tr: adj. 负有责任的；应作解释的
words.ex: He is accountable for his mistakes.
words.ex_cn: 他要为自己的错误负责。
words.en: If you are accountable to someone for something that you do, you are responsible for it and must be prepared to justify your actions to that person.

words.ex: He lived in a crude hut with no electricity.
words.ex_cn: 他住在一个没有电的简陋小屋里。
words.en: A crude substance or product is in its natural state and has not been processed or refined.

words.tr: v. 举例说明；例证；例示
words.ex: This example exemplifies the rule clearly.
words.ex_cn: 这个例子清楚地说明了这条规则。
words.en: To exemplify means to be a typical example of something or to give an example of something.

words.ex: The team's morale improved after they won the game.
words.ex_cn: 球队赢了比赛后，士气提升了。
words.en: Morale is the amount of confidence and cheerfulness that a group of people have.

words.ex: The king rode in a wooden carriage drawn by four horses.
words.ex_cn: 国王乘坐一辆由四匹马拉的木制四轮马车。
words.en: A carriage is a vehicle with four wheels that is pulled by horses and is used for carrying people.

words.ex: The two countries argued over territorial rights.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家就领土权利发生了争执。
words.en: Relating to the ownership of an area of land or sea.

words.ex: He inferred that she was tired from her yawns.
words.ex_cn: 他从她的哈欠推断出她很累。
words.en: If you infer that something is the case, you decide that it is true on the basis of information that you already have.

words.ex: The sentence has ambiguity because it can mean two things.
words.ex_cn: 这句话有歧义，因为它可以有两种意思。
words.en: If you say that there is ambiguity in something, you mean that it is unclear or confusing, or it can be understood in more than one way.

words.ex: The GPS can pinpoint your exact location.
words.ex_cn: GPS可以精准定位你的准确位置。
words.en: To pinpoint something means to locate or identify it precisely.

words.ex: The movie plot was cliched and predictable.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影的情节陈词滥调且可预测。
words.en: A clichéd phrase, idea, or work of art is one that has been used so often that it is no longer original or interesting.

words.tr: adj. 无可置疑的；决定性的；
words.ex: The evidence was conclusive.
words.ex_cn: 证据是无可置疑的。
words.en: If something is conclusive, it means that it proves something in a way that is certain and leaves no doubt.

words.ex: The merger of two companies created a bigger business.
words.ex_cn: 两家公司的合并创建了一家更大的企业。
words.en: A merger is the joining together of two separate companies or organizations so that they become one.

words.tr: v. 犯罪；做错事；“commit”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 忠诚的；
words.ex: He was committed for stealing a car.
words.ex_cn: 他因偷车而被定罪。
words.en: If you are committed to something, you are willing to give your time and energy to it because you believe in it.

words.tr: adj. 吱嘎作响的；发出刺耳声音的
words.ex: The door makes a squeaky sound when it opens.
words.ex_cn: 门打开时发出吱吱的声音。
words.en: Something that is squeaky makes high-pitched sounds.

words.ex: He kept his dignity even when he was poor.
words.ex_cn: 即使他很穷，他依然保持尊严。
words.en: Dignity is the quality of being worthy of honor or respect.

words.ex: I misplace my keys every morning.
words.ex_cn: 我每天早上都把钥匙弄丢。
words.en: If you misplace something, you lose it, usually only temporarily.

words.tr: adj. 最高的；至上的；最重要的；
words.ex: His safety is paramount.
words.ex_cn: 他的安全是最重要的。
words.en: Something that is paramount or of paramount importance is more important than anything else.

words.tr: adj. 失去知觉的；无意义的；无目的的；不明智的
words.ex: After the accident, he was senseless on the ground.
words.ex_cn: 事故发生后，他倒在地下，失去了知觉。
words.en: If you describe an action as senseless, you think it is wrong because it has no purpose and produces no benefit.

words.ex: The old man is frail and needs help to walk.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人瘦弱，需要帮助才能走路。
words.en: Someone who is frail is not very strong or healthy.

words.tr:
n. 尽力；尝试；
v. 尽力；奋力；
words.ex: His endeavor to finish the project took all his energy.
words.ex_cn: 他为完成这个项目付出了全部努力。
words.en: An endeavor is an attempt to do something, especially something new or original.

words.ex: The road was diverted around the park.
words.ex_cn: 这条路被改道绕过公园。
words.en: If you divert someone or something, you cause them to change direction or to go somewhere different.

words.ex: The book has a finite number of pages.
words.ex_cn: 这本书的页数是有限的。
words.en: Something that is finite has a definite fixed size or extent.

words.ex: Calling time a thief is a metaphor.
words.ex_cn: 把时间称为小偷是一种隐喻。
words.en: A metaphor is a figure of speech in which a word or phrase is applied to an object or action to which it is not literally applicable.

words.tr: adj. 统治的；支配的； v. “rule”的现在分词；
words.ex: The ruling class controls the government.
words.ex_cn: 统治阶级控制着政府。
words.en: A ruling is an official decision made by a judge or court, or a decision made by someone in authority.

words.tr: adj. 心智健全的；头脑清醒的；明智的
words.ex: He is still sane after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 事故发生后，他仍然神志清醒。
words.en: If someone is sane, they are able to think and behave in a normal and rational manner.

words.ex: The predominant color in the room is blue.
words.ex_cn: 房间里的主导颜色是蓝色。
words.en: If something is predominant, it is more important, noticeable, or powerful than the other things in a situation.

words.ex: The conversion of water into steam takes heat.
words.ex_cn: 水变成蒸汽需要热量。
words.en: The process of changing or causing something to change from one form to another.

words.ex: Drugs can relieve pain.
words.ex_cn: 药物可以减轻疼痛。
words.en: To relieve someone or something means to make a problem, pain, or unpleasant feeling less severe or to take it away completely.

words.ex: He stopped talking abruptly.
words.ex_cn: 他突然停止了说话。
words.en: Suddenly and unexpectedly.

words.ex: He bought a new mirror because of his vanity.
words.ex_cn: 他因为虚荣心买了一面新镜子。
words.en: The quality of being vain; excessive pride in or admiration of one's own appearance or achievements.

words.ex: He will initiate a new project next week.
words.ex_cn: 他将在下周发起一个新项目。
words.en: To initiate something means to start it or cause it to happen.

words.ex: He spoke with self-assurance during the interview.
words.ex_cn: 他在面试中自信地发言。
words.en: Self-assurance is confidence in your own abilities or character.

words.ex: There was a torrential rain last night.
words.ex_cn: 昨晚下了一场猛烈的雨。
words.en: Used to describe something that is like a torrent; very heavy or fast and powerful.

words.ex: I trusted my intuition and chose the right answer.
words.ex_cn: 我相信自己的直觉，选了正确的答案。
words.en: Intuition is the ability to understand or know something immediately, without the need for conscious reasoning.

words.ex: She tried to prevail on him to change his mind.
words.ex_cn: 她试图劝服他改变主意。
words.en: If a proposal, principle, or opinion prevails, it gains influence or is accepted, often after a struggle or argument.

words.ex: She is a vivacious girl who laughs loudly.
words.ex_cn: 她是一个活泼的女孩，笑得很响亮。
words.en: If you describe someone as vivacious, you mean that they are lively, exciting, and attractive.

words.ex: The farmer works hard to sustain his crops.
words.ex_cn: 这位农民努力维持他的庄稼。
words.en: To sustain something means to continue it or maintain it for a period of time.

words.ex: He walked sideways to avoid the puddle.
words.ex_cn: 他斜着走以避开水坑。
words.en: Moving or directed toward one side.

words.tr: adv. 逻辑上；合乎逻辑地；
words.ex: He solved the problem logically.
words.ex_cn: 他逻辑上解决了这个问题。
words.en: In a way that is reasonable and based on good judgment.

words.tr:
v. 夺取；一把抓住
n. 夺取；一把抓住；音乐片段
words.ex: He tried to snatch the bag from her hand.
words.ex_cn: 他试图从她手中抢走包。
words.en: If you snatch something, or if you snatch at it, you take it or pull it away quickly.

words.tr:
adj. 迅速的；敏捷的；快的；
n. 雨燕；
words.ex: The swift runner won the race.
words.ex_cn: 这位迅速的跑步者赢得了比赛。
words.en: moving or capable of moving at great speed, or happening within a very short time; fast.

words.ex: The repetition of the same words made the lesson boring.
words.ex_cn: 相同词语的重复让这堂课变得无聊。
words.en: The act of repeating something that has already been said or written.

words.ex: The project is ongoing.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目正在进行中。
words.en: An ongoing situation has been happening for quite a long time and seems likely to continue for some time in the future.

words.ex: The error is negligible.
words.ex_cn: 这个误差可以忽略。
words.en: If you describe something as negligible, you mean that it is so small or unimportant that it is not worth considering or worrying about.

words.ex: I sympathize with people who are hungry.
words.ex_cn: 我同情那些挨饿的人。
words.en: If you sympathize with someone who is in a bad situation, you feel sorry for them.

words.ex: He could not conceive a world without technology.
words.ex_cn: 他无法设想一个没有科技的世界。
words.en: To conceive means to form or devise a plan or idea in the mind; to become pregnant.

words.tr: adj. 造成创伤的；痛苦的；不愉快的
words.ex: The car accident was a traumatic experience.
words.ex_cn: 那场车祸是一次创伤性的经历。
words.en: If something is traumatic, it causes you severe emotional distress and anxiety.

words.ex: The life span of a dog is about 10 to 15 years.
words.ex_cn: 狗的寿命大约是10到15年。
words.en: The length of time for which a person or animal lives or a thing functions.

words.tr: adv. 无意地；不知不觉地
words.ex: He unconsciously tapped his foot while waiting.
words.ex_cn: 他等的时候无意识地敲着脚。
words.en: If you do something unconsciously, you do it without being aware of it.

words.tr: adj. 无知的；缺乏知识的
words.ex: He was ignorant of the basic rules.
words.ex_cn: 他对基本规则一无所知。
words.en: If you describe someone as ignorant, you mean that they do not know things they should know. If someone is ignorant of a fact, they do not know it.

words.tr: n. 层次体系；等级制度；
words.ex: The company has a clear hierarchy from manager to worker.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司有一个从经理到员工的明确层次体系。
words.en: A hierarchy is a system in which people or things are arranged according to their importance.

words.ex: He is intellectually curious about science.
words.ex_cn: 他在智力上对科学充满好奇。
words.en: In a way that relates to the intellect or is characterized by intellectual activity.

words.ex: Her performance was phenomenal.
words.ex_cn: 她的表现非常非凡。
words.en: If you describe something as phenomenal, you think it is extremely good or impressive.

words.ex: He asked for a quotation for the new computer.
words.ex_cn: 他询问了新电脑的报价。
words.en: A quotation is a sentence or phrase taken from a book, poem, play, etc., which is repeated by someone else, or a statement of the current price of something.

words.ex: The apple's flesh is sweet and juicy.
words.ex_cn: 苹果的果肉又甜又多汁。
words.en: The soft substance consisting of muscle and fat that is found between the skin and bones of an animal or a human.

words.ex: He poured milk from a jug.
words.ex_cn: 他从一个水壶里倒牛奶。
